key_insight: Plaquette converts realistic hardware noise models directly into fault-tolerant logical-performance estimates, avoiding the inaccuracies of Pauli-only assumptions.
engineering_relevance: It helps quantum hardware teams decide which imperfections to suppress by predicting architecture-level impact from the device’s actual open-system physics.
method: Represents hardware noise as Kraus operators, Hamiltonian-Lindblad dynamics, or reconstructed quantum channels.
Automatically compiles each noise model into the right simulator: stabilizer, XPauli, near-Clifford, or full-state.
Supports exact or approximate evaluation of logical performance for FTQC architectures.
evidence_signal: The XPauli and near-Clifford samplers were validated against full-state simulation and matched within statistical uncertainty on leakage, scattering, and heating models, while Pauli twirling could deviate depending on the noise process.
watch_item: Accurate results depend on having a faithful hardware noise model and on the computational cost of moving beyond stabilizer-only simulation.
paper_title: Plaquette: A hardware-aware design platform for fault-tolerant quantum computers
